To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Open Baton is a MANO framework that allows the deployment of NFV services on different types of infrastructure.

Open Baton is able to support the deployment of container based services on MEC nodes, and that this is achieved by extending the MANO framework with a new plugin that allows the management of containers and their deployment on MEC nodes.

(a) we have developed a prototype of an NFV-based MEC platform that can support the deployment of containerized network functions; and (b) we have evaluated its performance and scalability in a real environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1) how to provide a common framework for the deployment and management of container-based services at the edge of a network?
the development of an architecture for the deployment of containerized network services at the edge of a network, and the validation of such architecture in a realistic scenario.
the development of an architecture and its validation through a proof of concept prototype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Open Baton is the only open source MANO framework that provides a complete set of tools to deploy container-based network functions in MEC nodes.
OpenBaton is the first open source framework that supports the deployment of network services based on containers in a multi-access edge computing scenario.
this paper shows the feasibility of a container-based MEC architecture, which is a promising solution for the deployment of 5G services in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present a novel approach for deploying container-based NFV services in 5G-ready networks, which is based on the OpenBaton MANO framework and which can be used for deploying container-based services at the network edge.
we have prototyped a MEC node, based on the ETSI MEC standard, and deployed it at the edge of a 4G/LTE network.
Open Baton has been extended to support the orchestration and management of containerized network functions, including their placement in edge nodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
containerization can be successfully used to deploy NFV-based network services even in edge environments.
the proposed architecture can be used as a reference implementation for the integration of containerized network services in 5G-ready infrastructures.
container-based network services can be deployed in MEC nodes and can be managed in a similar way to standard virtualized network services, leveraging on the Open Baton MANO framework.
